newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet fuel, diesel up on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet fuel, diesel up on tight supplies.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel soared on strong regional demand on Tuesday with diesel trading at a new five-year high, industry sources said.
A European major and a Singapore traded 150,000-barrels at $31.50 per barrel, fob, loading December 11-15. It was 70 cents higher than the previous high chalked up in mid November.

Gas oil prices in Singapore have recently risen sharply due to renewed buying interest from China following lower crude runs. China is expected to buy an extra 100,000-tonnes for December arrival to total 600,000-tonnes, traders said.
Dec gas oil swaps traded a high of $30.94 late in the day.
Jet fuel rose sharply as traders covered earlier sales commitments to North Asia, they said.

Premiums in Japan have risen by about 20-30 cents over the past few days. Japan recently bought a 30,000-tonne cargo at a premium of close to $2.00 a barrel over spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
Dec jet fuel swaps traded to an intraday high of $33.45 per barrel but eased later to about $33.30, brokers said.
Taiwan awarded its January 1-15 buy tender of 250,000 barrels of unleaded 95-octane reformate to a European major around $26.80 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan, traders said.

Although much higher than Taiwan's December purchase above $25.50, the naphtha/mogas spread was under pressure on naphtha's strength. On paper, December gasoline was only $2.00 above naphtha at $23.30/$23.50.

Singapore naphtha edged up on tight prompt supplies. A major sold a cargo last week at $1.10-$1.15, fob over Singapore spot for 250,000 barrels of light naphtha lifting mid-Dec. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
